name: Lahore Fort and Alamgiri Gate
assumptions: Gate height is photo-derived: bastion merlons about 20.6 m and finials 28.6 m above the gate floor, gate floor 2.8 m above the road; no published height was found beyond an unsourced Wikipedia figure of 30 m, and the total here is 31.4 m above the road.
Scale taken from the OSM gate width of 46.1 m on the frontal photo; centre block elements carry a 7 percent correction for standing further back.
Bastion lobes, petals and merlons set at 14 for a full circle from about 7 visible per front view; the count is not published and a lobe is centred on the front by choice.
Loophole positions are staggered on alternate lobes in three tiers, matching the photos in pattern rather than slit by slit.
Iwan arch and door drawn with the kit's Mughal four-centred arch; the bent passage inside the gate and the door leaves are not modelled, the door reads as a dark panel set back.
Square buttress towers: plan 4.9 by 11.5 m estimated from the frontal and oblique photos, not separately traced in OSM; the outer faces at 23.9 m from the axis are 0.85 m beyond the OSM half width.

Podium colour is unresolved: dd_baradari and graana_gate show pink-red faces, madain_gate, pakheritage and dream_gate show cream; none of the photos carries a date and a search found no record of repainting, so cream (the majority) is a choice, not a verified current state.
Podium blocks and ramp: extent from photos, inner edge set on the drum foot; paving is a plain pink-grey tile standing in for the real slabs.

Bastion radius 6.3 m at the foot, 5.75 to 5.15 m on the shaft and centres 32 m apart come from the frontal photo; OSM salients trace about 7.3 m radius and 30.8 m apart, but that outline is less consistent with the photographed proportions.
Straight flanks join each half-round drum to the curtain; the rear of the drums is not visible in any photo.
Centre parapet: 16 panels and 23 tiny crenels are counted approximately from small photos.
Interior footprints whose corners fall outside the inner rampart face are clipped to it, and strips along the wall that leave little area are dropped.
Inner court behind the gate is the OSM ring extruded plain, 8.5 m above the gate floor, height unknown.
Ramparts follow the dossier OSM ring simplified to 3.5 m: heights 18 m south of the gate, 15 m north of it and along the Picture Wall (dossier 15 m), 13 m elsewhere; the rest are unknown.
Rampart thickness 6 m and batter 0.9 m are estimates; the fort interior is a single level 6 m above the road, though the real fort has several terraces.
South half of the west wall drawn as two tiers of arched recesses with merlons from a distance photo; bay width estimated at 7.4 m.

Picture Wall: 116 panels (dossier) drawn as alternating tile-framed niches and tile panels along the north wall, a repeating pattern standing in for 116 distinct mosaics; panel layout is representative only.
North wall towers come from small OSM ring nubs; their radius of about 3.3 m and height are estimates.
Interior buildings are OSM footprints extruded: 6.5 m default, a few named buildings estimated; ruins 2.5 m. Forms beyond the footprint are not modelled, except the Naulakha curved roof.
Moti Masjid has no OSM footprint under that name in the area fetched and is left out; Akbari Gate is a plain brick mass at its OSM plan, 16 m high.
Colours are photo estimates apart from the dossier cream tints; night amber glow matches one night photo and no lighting scheme is documented.
